answer: Let every identity mature in the reef before it earns: a newborn agent is plankton, paid nothing for its first epochs no matter how much it works, and payout then grows with the square of its age, sealed at birth in an onyx ledger no one can backdate. Age accrues only on epochs where the identity completes work a stranger verifies, so a clone cannot wander in, idle, and age for free. A farm spawning a thousand clones must wait out a thousand separate maturation clocks in real time, and each clock ticks only while its clone works — time, unlike compute, cannot be cloned.
